one_line_for_the_editor: The first corpus paper in which the E-path write operator itself has trainable parameters: consolidation of a text memory bank is a multi-step tool-use policy trained by GRPO against downstream agent success. At deployment nothing but the bank moves, so it is (U-E) — but the operator that performs (U-E) was produced by gradient descent, which no previous E-path paper required.

problem_stated.as_the_paper_frames_it: Two named problems. (i) A CONSOLIDATION problem: 'existing methods typically couple acquisition and consolidation into a single online update process, so each update is made with limited evidence from the current session. This makes it difficult to discover recurring patterns, abstract reusable procedures that generalize across sessions, resolve contradictions, or prune redundant entries.' [Auto-Dreamer §1, p.1-2]. (ii) A MEMORY-UTILITY problem: 'RL-trained memory methods optimize online construction or retrieval rather than offline consolidation under an explicit downstream utility objective, so they do not directly learn which memories are load-bearing, which entries are redundant, or how to trade off success against memory compactness.' [Auto-Dreamer §1, p.2]
problem_stated.the_framing_move: Long-term memory is redefined away from retrieval: 'long-term memory is not merely a retrieval cache for past entities or user preferences; it is the mechanism by which an agent converts raw experience into reusable procedures, environment knowledge, and behavioral priors that improve future decision making. A memory system must therefore solve two distinct problems: it must rapidly acquire useful information from each new trajectory, and it must periodically reorganize accumulated experience into a form that is compact, non-redundant, and useful for future tasks.' [Auto-Dreamer §1, p.1]
problem_stated.the_theoretical_borrowing_and_its_discla: 'We take inspiration from complementary learning systems (CLS) theory of human memory, in which a fast hippocampal system encodes individual episodes and a slower neocortical system gradually extracts shared structure across episodes [17, 12, 18]. We adopt CLS not as a biological claim about language models, but as an operational design principle for separating fast acquisition from slow cross-session consolidation.' [Auto-Dreamer §1, p.2]
problem_stated.note_writer_remark: [note-writer] This is the first paper in the corpus that borrows the CLS argument, cites its primary sources, AND prints the disclaimer that the book demanded of the whole line (-> ch23). The disclaimer is not hedging; it is exactly the distinction ch23 §23.8 asks readers to draw between 'supports' and 'is analogous to'.

inherited_open_question.verdict: stated-but-not-quoted; and it functionally answers a Letta STC open question without citing it as one
inherited_open_question.what_the_paper_says_it_inherits: A gap attributed to a named set of RL-trained memory papers, in the paper's own words rather than theirs: 'However, these methods primarily focus on teaching the model to extract and organize knowledge from its input, rather than on improving downstream agentic task performance. Later methods bridge this gap: UMEM [37] jointly trains memory extraction and management with GRPO under an online single-step interface, and MemRL [40] trains the agent to retrieve the correct memory at decision time. Nevertheless, all of these operate online: memory updates are interleaved with task execution, so consolidation evidence is limited to the current session. Auto-Dreamer addresses a complementary problem, operating offline over a bank accumulated across many sessions with access to the full memory bank and raw source trajectories.' [Auto-Dreamer §2 'RL-trained memory managers', p.3]
inherited_open_question.the_nearest_named_counterpart: LightMem is designated the architectural predecessor and the specific difference is named: 'LightMem [5] combines an online writer with periodic offline consolidation, but implements consolidation as a fixed prompted pipeline with per-entry CRUD decisions. Auto-Dreamer instead performs region rewriting: it treats a selected working region as read-only evidence, then uses a learned multi-step tool-using consolidator to synthesize a fresh compact replacement set that abstracts across sessions and supersedes the original region.' [Auto-Dreamer §2 'Offline computation and sleep-time memory', p.3]. §5.1 repeats the designation: LightMem is 'the closest architectural counterpart to our method' [p.6].
inherited_open_question.the_letta_stc_link: Letta `Sleep-time Compute` is cited exactly once, in the same paragraph: 'Sleep-time compute [14] pre-computes over persistent context before queries arrive, amortizing reasoning across future interactions.' [Auto-Dreamer §2, p.3]. No open question of Letta STC's is quoted. But the paper's deployment regime is a direct, unattributed answer to Letta STC's second future-work item — 'real-world LLM use cases can be more complex, with multiple rounds of interaction and context modifications between rounds ... Future work should extend sleep-time compute paradigm to more elegantly handle these scenarios' [Letta STC §7, p.13]. Auto-Dreamer's continual-memory regime is exactly that: consolidation fires every k completed sessions over a stream of 117-660 tasks [Auto-Dreamer App. B.2, p.16].

core_mechanism.one_line_unified: Auto-Dreamer instantiates (U-E) alone at deployment, with three specialisations: $\mathrm{wr}$ is REGION REPLACEMENT (a selected subset of the store is deleted and superseded by a synthesized set, entries outside it untouched), $S(\cdot;B_s)$ is a TRAINED multi-step tool-use policy rather than a prompt, and $\mathrm{ret}$ is a genuine budgeted top-$K$ retriever rather than the identity. $\Theta$ and $W$ of every model in the serving path are frozen; the only gradient in the paper lands on the parameters of the write operator, in an offline RL phase that precedes deployment.

equations_unified.paper_form: $\mathrm{Read}(q;\mathcal{B}) = \text{Top-}K_{e\in\mathcal{B}}\cos(\phi(q), \phi(n_e\oplus s_e))$ — the LEFT half of the paper's Eq. 1
equations_unified.gloss: Unlike Letta STC, $\mathrm{ret}$ here is not the identity. $\phi$ is a frozen sentence encoder (Qwen2.5-3B last-token hidden state, 2048-d, FAISS IndexFlatIP over L2-normalised vectors [App. B.1.6, p.16; App. B.2, p.18]). $K$ is not a constant: 'K is the largest ranked prefix fitting the token budget' [§3, p.4]. The realised budget is top-$k=3$ with a 1500-token cap at task start, plus the top-1 entry re-queried and appended every 8 environment steps [App. B.2, p.18].

equations_unified.latex: \textbf{sleep write (U-E):}\qquad E_{k+1} \;=\; \mathrm{wr}\big(E_k,\ \hat c_k\big) \;=\; \big(E_k \setminus \mathcal{W}_k\big)\ \cup\ \hat c_k, \qquad \hat c_k \;=\; S_{\theta_C}\big(\mathcal{W}_k,\ \mathcal{T}_{\mathcal{W}_k};\ B_s\big)
equations_unified.paper_form: $\mathrm{Write}(\mathcal{B},\mathcal{R},\mathcal{T}_{\mathcal{R}}) = (\mathcal{B}\setminus\mathcal{R})\cup C_\theta(\mathcal{R},\mathcal{T}_{\mathcal{R}})$, with $C_\theta(\mathcal{R},\mathcal{T}_{\mathcal{R}})=\mathcal{S}$ and $\mathcal{B}^\star=(\mathcal{B}\setminus\mathcal{R})\cup\mathcal{S}$ — the RIGHT half of the paper's Eq. 1
equations_unified.gloss: $\mathcal{W}_k$ is this note's replacement for the paper's working region $\mathcal{R}$ (the book reserves $R$ for reward and $\mathcal{R}_k$ for the (U-$\Theta$) training set). THE SEMANTICS ARE THE CONTRIBUTION: the region is read-only evidence, not an object edited in place, and its entries do not survive unless re-synthesized. The paper's own statement: 'entries in $\mathcal{R}$ are treated as read-only evidence rather than edited in place, and entries outside $\mathcal{R}$ are left unchanged' [§3, p.4]; 'old entries do not persist by default, and information survives only if it is re-synthesized into the replacement set. As a result, abstraction, deduplication, contradiction resolution, and omission-based forgetting become default behaviors.' [§1, p.2]

equations_unified.latex: \textbf{working-region selection at deployment:}\qquad \mathcal{W}_k \;=\; \{\text{entries written in the last }k_{\text{cad}}\text{ sessions}\}\ \cup\ \{\text{older entries retrieved by the task agent in the same interval}\}
equations_unified.gloss: The selector is a fixed rule, not learned. It is the one place where wake-time behaviour feeds back into what sleep touches: an old entry re-enters the rewrite candidate set only by having been RETRIEVED. Entries never retrieved and never re-written are frozen forever — the store has an unswept tail that the paper does not measure.
equations_unified.source: [Auto-Dreamer §4.2, p.5: 'We trigger consolidation every k sessions and define the working region R as the union of entries newly written during the interval and older entries retrieved by the task agent during the same interval... Entries outside R are left unchanged but may enter a future working region if retrieved in subsequent tasks.']

equations_unified.latex: \textbf{the operator is a bounded tool-use rollout:}\qquad S_{\theta_C}: \ \big(\mathcal{W},\ \mathcal{T}_{\mathcal{W}}\big)\ \longmapsto\ \hat c, \qquad \text{at most } T_{\max}\ \text{turns over } \{\texttt{search\_memory},\ \texttt{check\_memory},\ \texttt{get\_source\_trace},\ \texttt{synthesize},\ \texttt{terminate}\}
equations_unified.gloss: $S$ is no longer a single prompted generation. It is an agent loop with four tools plus a terminator, one tool call per turn, ending on `terminate` or on the turn budget. `get_source_trace` is what makes the operator PROVENANCE-GROUNDED: the consolidator can re-read the raw action-observation trace that produced an entry, which the task agent itself never sees ('Raw trajectories in T are not retrieved by the task agent at decision time but remain available to the consolidator as provenance evidence.' [§3, p.4]).
equations_unified.source: [Auto-Dreamer §4.1, p.4-5; §4, p.4; tool list verbatim in App. E.2, p.23: 'search_memory(query, k=5) / check_memory(ids=[...]) (up to 30 ids) / get_source_trace(id) / synthesize(source_ids, type, name, summary, details?, steps?) / terminate()']

equations_unified.latex: \textbf{outer loop — the operator's own parameters (NOT sleep-time compute):}\qquad \theta_C \;\leftarrow\; \mathrm{GRPO}\big(\theta_C;\ \{r_g\}_{g=1}^{G}\big), \qquad \hat c_g \;=\; S_{\theta_C}\big(\mathcal{W},\mathcal{T}_{\mathcal{W}}\big),\ \ g=1,\ldots,G
equations_unified.paper_form: Algorithm 1, p.6, lines 4-8; 'We train the consolidator $C_\theta$ with GRPO [22]. The writer, retriever, task agent, and memory-token budget are fixed across rollouts; only the consolidator parameters $\theta$ are updated. The consolidator is initialized from Qwen3-14B.' [§4.3, p.6]
equations_unified.gloss: THIS IS THE PAPER'S NOVELTY AND IT IS NOT A SLEEP-TIME UPDATE. It has the shape of (U-$\Theta$) — AdamW on 14B parameters — but the $\Theta$ it moves belongs to the WRITE OPERATOR, not to any model on the read path, and it is moved once, offline, before deployment. In book terms: $\mathrm{wr}$ and $S(\cdot;B_s)$ acquire parameters. The book's (U-E) leaves both operators unspecified, so this is an instantiation the canonical form permits but which no previous corpus paper used.
equations_unified.source: [Auto-Dreamer §4.3, p.5-6; Algorithm 1, p.6; App. B.3 Table 6, p.19]

equations_unified.latex: \textbf{reward:}\qquad r_g \;=\; U_{\mathcal{V}}(\hat c_g)\ +\ \alpha_{\mathrm{cf}}\, r_{\mathrm{cf}}(\hat c_g;\mathcal{V}), \qquad U_{\mathcal{V}}(\hat c) \;=\; \frac{1}{|\mathcal{V}|}\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}} \mathrm{Return}(v;\hat c), \qquad r_{\mathrm{cf}}(\hat c_g;\mathcal{V}) \;=\; U_{\mathcal{V}}(\hat c_g)\ -\ \mathbb{E}_{\tilde c\sim q_{\rho_{\mathrm{mask}}}(\cdot\mid \hat c_g)}\big[U_{\mathcal{V}}(\tilde c)\big]
equations_unified.paper_form: the paper's Eq. 2 and Eq. 3, p.6, written with $\mathcal{S}_g$ where this note writes $\hat c_g$ and with bare $\alpha$ and $\rho$
equations_unified.gloss: The second term is a leave-random-out counterfactual: $q_{\rho_{\mathrm{mask}}}$ masks a fixed fraction of the synthesized entries uniformly at random and the expectation is estimated with $M_g$ Monte Carlo samples. The paper's reading of the three regimes is explicit: 'masking load-bearing entries lowers performance, masking redundant entries has little effect because duplicate information remains, and masking harmful entries can improve performance, making $r_{\mathrm{cf}}$ negative.' [§4.3, p.6]. Realised values: $\alpha_{\mathrm{cf}}=0.5$ ('MC-dropout weight'), $\rho_{\mathrm{mask}}=0.5$ ('MC-dropout: drop fraction'), sample fraction 0.25, min $N$ 1 [Table 6, p.19].
equations_unified.discrepancy: Table 6 also lists 'Format-penalty weight 0.5', a reward component that appears in NO equation in the paper. Eq. 2 as printed is therefore not the reward that was optimised. See unfavorable_facts and todo_verify.
equations_unified.source: [Auto-Dreamer Eq. 2 and Eq. 3, §4.3, p.6; Table 6 'Reward shaping', p.19]

equations_unified.latex: \textbf{training-time credit assignment (local bank):}\qquad E^{\star}_g \;=\; \hat c_g \qquad \text{(the whole store during scoring IS the replacement set)}
equations_unified.gloss: At training time the rewritten region is not composed back into a bank; each candidate is evaluated ALONE. 'This aligns the unit of credit assignment with the unit produced by the policy: reward is assigned directly to the replacement set, rather than to a full bank whose performance may be explained by memories not produced by the current rollout.' [§4.3, p.6]. This is a deliberate train/deploy mismatch and the paper names it as such — 'The local-bank training objective (§4.3) is a surrogate for deployment-time bank composition... the formal relationship between local-bank ranking and full-bank ranking is not characterized.' [App. A, p.15]
equations_unified.source: [Auto-Dreamer §4.3, p.5-6; Algorithm 1 line 6, p.6; App. A, p.15]

equations_unified.latex: \textbf{frozen layers at deployment:}\qquad \Theta_{k+1}=\Theta_k\ \ \forall k, \qquad W_t = W_{t-1}\ \ \forall t, \qquad \theta_C\ \text{frozen after training}
equations_unified.gloss: Stated by the paper in one sentence: 'The task agent, retriever, writer, memory schema, and token budget are all fixed; only the consolidator parameters are updated during training, and only the memory bank is updated after deployment.' [§4, p.4]. And in the preliminaries: 'Offline consolidation leaves the task agent, retriever, and memory schema fixed; it transforms $\mathcal{B}$ into a post-consolidation bank $\mathcal{B}^\star$.' [§3, p.3-4]. This single sentence is what settles the path assignment — see discriminant_verdict.

equations_unified.latex: \textbf{fast acquisition (the other timescale):}\qquad E \;\leftarrow\; E\ \cup\ \mathrm{writer}(\tau_t) \qquad \text{after every session } \tau_t, \ \ \text{append-only}
equations_unified.gloss: The writer is deliberately handicapped so that all reorganisation is the consolidator's job: 'The writer is intentionally local and append-only: it does not search the existing bank, compare entries across sessions, or rewrite old memories. This favors plasticity—new experience is recorded immediately and cheaply. Slower cross-session operations (merging, abstraction, correction, compression, forgetting) are delegated to the consolidator.' [§4.1, p.4]. The writer emits typed `INSERT_SEMANTIC` / `INSERT_PROCEDURAL` blocks parsed verbatim into the bank [App. E.1, p.21].

the_two_timescales_named.fast: per-session prompted writer, append-only, fires after every session [§4.1, p.4]
the_two_timescales_named.slow: learned consolidator, fires every $k_{\text{cad}}$ completed sessions: $k_{\text{cad}}=10$ (ScienceWorld), $8$ (ALFWorld), $5$ (WebArena) [App. B.2, p.16]
the_two_timescales_named.third_and_unnamed: [note-writer] the operator-training timescale, which is neither fast nor slow in the paper's sense but a one-off outer loop preceding both. The paper's own two-timescale label undercounts by one, and the uncounted one is where the gradient is.

what_is_NOT_in_the_mechanism: No weight update of any model on the read path. Task agent, writer, retriever, embedder are all frozen [§4, p.4]. Whole-text grep: 'LoRA' 0 hits, 'fine-tun' 0 hits, 'gradient' 0 hits.

No merge, no per-entry edit, no CRUD. The paper defines itself against exactly that: 'In CRUD-style memory managers, existing memories persist unless the controller explicitly edits or deletes them, so consolidation is expressed as many local retention decisions. In region rewriting, the unit of rewriting is a region rather than an individual entry' [§4.1, p.4-5].

No rollback, no versioning, no history of superseded entries. Entries leave the active bank when not re-synthesized. The evaluation logs distinguish 'end-of-run active and retired bank sizes' [App. B.2, p.18], so retired entries are tracked — but no retired-bank number is printed anywhere.

No verification of the synthesized entries against ground truth. The only correctness pressure is downstream task return during TRAINING; at deployment nothing checks a rewrite. The synthesizer prompt asks for grounding ('Every synthesized entry must cite source_ids drawn from the reference bank' [App. E.2, p.23]) but citation is not verification.
No learned region selector, no learned retriever. Both are fixed rules; the paper lists joint optimisation of retrieval and consolidation as future work [§6, p.11].
No cross-user or cross-deployment state. The bank is scoped to a run (`LanceDB partitioned by run_id` [App. B.2, p.18]). Personalisation is not discussed.

No full-context arm. Whole-text grep for 'full-context' and 'full context' returns 0 hits. The only memoryless comparator is 'No memory', which receives 'only the current observation and the task instruction' [App. B.1, p.15].

outer_vs_inner.headline: This is the first E-path paper in the corpus whose outer-loop column is NOT empty. Exactly one object is learned by gradient descent — the parameters of the write operator — and it is learned before deployment, on one environment, and then frozen. Everything on the read path is frozen throughout. So the table has three columns in effect: trained-once-offline (the consolidator), moved-at-sleep (the bank), and never-moved (everything else).

outer_vs_inner.reader_takeaway: [note-writer] For the monograph this changes a teaching fact. ch14's note recorded that the E-path could be demonstrated end to end without a single backward pass, which made it the right first stop before the W- and $\Theta$-path chapters. That is no longer true of the E-path's frontier. Auto-Dreamer's contribution cannot be read without Part I's RL module (→ ch05): GRPO, group-relative advantage, reward shaping, and a counterfactual credit term are all load-bearing. The E-path has acquired an outer loop — not on the model that answers, but on the operator that writes.

update_layer.instantiates: (U-E) at deployment, and only (U-E). The gradient in the paper is not a sleep-time update at all: it is an outer loop that produces the operator which later performs (U-E).
how_this_paper_differs_from_the_canonica: $\mathrm{wr}$ = REGION REPLACEMENT, a fourth write species for the corpus. ch14 recorded destructive overwrite of a single block (Letta) and concatenation across parallel trajectories; ch15 recorded per-message CRUD (Mem0), episodic append plus periodic community refresh (Zep), and pure union with no pruning (ReasoningBank). Auto-Dreamer's $\mathrm{wr}$ is $(E\setminus\mathcal{W})\cup\hat c$ — destructive on a SELECTED SUBSET and inert elsewhere. The paper's claim for this choice is structural rather than empirical: 'This replacement semantics makes compactness structural rather than auxiliary' [§1, p.2], and Table 2 supports it — the untrained pipeline alone shrinks the bank 6.02× / 7.35× / 10.82× versus writer-only [본서 산술 from Table 2, p.9].

$S$ IS PARAMETERISED. In every prior E-path paper $S(\cdot;B_s)$ was a frozen model plus a fixed prompt. Here it is a policy $S_{\theta_C}$ whose weights were moved by RL against downstream task return. The book's (U-E) admits this — it never said $S$ was a prompt — but no corpus paper had used the freedom. This is the single most consequential mechanical fact in the note.

$S$ IS A TOOL-USE AGENT WITH READ ACCESS BELOW THE STORE. `get_source_trace` lets the consolidator re-read raw action-observation traces that the task agent can never retrieve [§3, p.4; App. E.2, p.23]. In book terms the sleep procedure sees a substrate the wake path does not: $S$ acts on $(\mathcal{W}, \mathcal{T}_{\mathcal{W}})$ while $\mathrm{ret}$ acts on $E$ alone. Letta STC's $S$ saw only the context it was rewriting.

$\mathrm{ret}$ IS A REAL RETRIEVER, unlike ch14's identity map. Top-$K$ cosine over frozen 2048-d embeddings with a token budget, realised as top-3 at task start plus top-1 every 8 environment steps [Eq. 1, §3, p.4; App. B.2, p.18]. Consequence for the book's accounting: the wake-time prompt contribution is BOUNDED BY THE RETRIEVAL BUDGET AND IS THE SAME FOR EVERY ARM. Bank size therefore does not enter the wake prompt term at all — it enters through retrieval precision. This is a different economics from ch14/ch15 and the chapter must say so.

$k$ ACTUALLY RANGES OVER MANY ROUNDS. ch14 recorded that Letta STC's round index never exceeds 1 and that $\rho$ was therefore out of scope by construction. Auto-Dreamer fires the consolidator repeatedly across a task stream — [본서 산술] roughly $660/10=66$ rounds on ScienceWorld, $274/8\approx34$ on ALFWorld, $117/5\approx23$ on WebArena, using the pool sizes of Table 5 (p.18) and the cadences of App. B.2 (p.16). The multi-round regime that ch14 listed as Letta STC's open question is executed here. What is still missing is a measurement of per-round degradation — see cost_table.rho.

THE STORE HAS AN UNSWEPT TAIL. Only entries newly written or recently RETRIEVED enter a working region [§4.2, p.5]. An entry that is never retrieved is never reconsidered, so it neither improves nor is pruned; it persists as dead weight in $C_{\text{cap}}$ and as a competitor in the retrieval index. The paper does not measure the size of this tail, and its logging distinguishes active from retired banks [App. B.2, p.18] without printing either decomposition.

other_layers.U-W: not touched. $W$ does not exist in the architectures used and is never mentioned.
other_layers.U-Theta: not touched ON THE READ PATH. The paper never fine-tunes, adapts, or edits the task agent, the writer, or the retriever. The one gradient computation in the paper updates $\theta_C$, the write operator's own parameters, in an offline phase that ends before any evaluation begins. Using the book's Rosetta row 'model redeployment ↔ one (U-$\Theta$)': the deployed artefact that answers queries is NEVER redeployed; the artefact that is redeployed is the memory service.

update_layer.ordering: Three clocks, in this order. (0) OUTER, once, offline: GRPO on $\theta_C$ over ScienceWorld regions. (1) FAST, after every session: append-only writer emits typed entries with provenance pointers. (2) SLOW, every $k_{\mathrm{cad}}$ sessions: $S_{\theta_C}$ rewrites the working region; $E_k \to E_{k+1}$. Read happens between (1) and (2) and after (2), never during. Clock (0) runs exactly once and on one environment; clocks (1) and (2) interleave for the life of the stream.
update_layer.why_this_is_E_and_not_Theta: One sentence of the paper settles it: 'The task agent, retriever, writer, memory schema, and token budget are all fixed; only the consolidator parameters are updated during training, and only the memory bank is updated after deployment.' [§4, p.4]. A second confirms the scope: 'Offline consolidation leaves the task agent, retriever, and memory schema fixed; it transforms $\mathcal{B}$ into a post-consolidation bank $\mathcal{B}^\star$.' [§3, p.3-4]. The rewrite target is a memory region. $\Theta$ does not move. The path is $E$.

Whole-text greps: 'FLOP' 0 hits, 'latency' 0 hits, 'GPU-hour' 0 hits, 'dollar' 0 hits, 'seconds' 0 hits. The word 'cost' occurs seven times and EVERY occurrence refers to memory-bank size in tokens ('Success–cost tradeoff' Fig. 3a caption; 'retrieval-time memory cost' §5.2 p.8 and Fig. 3 caption p.8; 'comparable or smaller memory cost' §5.3 p.8; 'without a measurable cost in task success' §5.4 p.9; 'success–cost plane' §5.2 p.8; 'success–cost tradeoff' App. I p.30). There is no compute-cost quantity in the paper.
B_s.what_IS_reported_instead: Ordinal and structural knobs only: consolidation cadence $k_{\mathrm{cad}}\in\{1,5,8,10,20\}$ [App. B.2 p.16; §5.4 p.9]; one tool call per turn with a $T_{\max}$ that is never given a number [Alg. 1, p.6; App. E.2, p.23]; `search_memory(query, k=5)` and `check_memory` 'up to 30 ids' [App. E.2, p.23]; consolidator backbone Qwen3-14B [§4.3, p.6].
B_s.the_sharpest_fact: The paper MEASURED $B_s$ and did not print it. App. B.2 (p.18) states that `summary.json` reports 'total wall-clock time, and per-role LLM call and token counts', and that `dreamer_calls.jsonl` logs writer/dreamer events per task. The dreamer's token count is therefore in the authors' logs. It is in no table, no figure axis, and no sentence.
B_s.training_side: Also absent in absolute terms, but bounded by configuration [본서 산술]: 200 training steps × 16 prompts/batch × 8 rollouts/group = 25,600 consolidator rollouts, each up to $T_{\max}$ turns at ≤2,048 new tokens/turn, and each scored by running a frozen Qwen3.5-9B task agent over the evaluation set $\mathcal{V}$ plus $M_{\mathrm{cf}}$ masked variants ('Evaluations per sample 12'). Hardware: 8×H100 80GB. No hours are given [Table 6, p.19; App. B.2 'Hardware', p.18]. Mark any absolute derived from this as [본서 산술].

L_w.detail: No wall-clock, TTFT, ms/token, or throughput number for the serving path. 'latency' appears 0 times in the whole text. The paper reports no wake-time cost proxy of any kind — not even a generated-token axis, which ch14's paper at least had.
L_w.the_one_wake_quantity_that_IS_pinned: The retrieval budget, which caps the wake-time memory prompt for every arm identically: top-$k=3$ entries under a 1500-token budget at task start, plus the top-1 entry appended to the user message every 8 environment steps [App. B.2, p.18]. Episode step caps: 50 (ALFWorld), 100 (ScienceWorld), 300 (WebArena) [Table 5, p.18]. [본서 산술] the per-episode injected-memory upper bound is therefore 1500 tokens plus at most $\lfloor 50/8\rfloor=6$, $\lfloor 100/8\rfloor=12$, $\lfloor 300/8\rfloor=37$ additional single entries — identical across arms, independent of bank size.
L_w.consequence: [note-writer] The book must not translate '#Tok.' into a wake-latency saving. Under this paper's own protocol a 370,874-token bank and a 927-token bank inject the same bounded number of tokens per query. Where bank size actually bites is retrieval PRECISION (which three entries win the slots), embedding-index size, and rerank work — not prefill.

C_cap.why_absent_is_still_the_right_word: The book's unit is bytes per session or per user [S0-DESIGN §2.4; STC-STYLE-NOTATION §1.2]. This paper reports no bytes and no per-user quantity; its banks are per-run (`LanceDB partitioned by run_id` [App. B.2, p.18]) and its unit is tokens. ch26's finding E1 — no discriminant-passing paper reports $C_{\text{cap}}$ in per-user bytes — therefore SURVIVES this paper.
C_cap.what_the_paper_DOES_report_and_why_it_ma: The most complete state-capacity reporting in the corpus: final active bank size in tokens, for ELEVEN systems, across THREE domains, in the same table as the quality number [Table 1, p.7], plus a second full column set for the controlled regime, plus per-arm ablation columns [Table 2, p.9], plus two case studies giving entry COUNTS as well as tokens [Table 23, p.30; Table 24, p.31]. No previous corpus paper printed a state-size column at all.
C_cap.entry_level_data_for_a_bytes_conversion: App. I gives 14 active entries / 716 tokens for Auto-Dreamer and 265 entries / 17,512 tokens for LightMem at episode 90 of a ScienceWorld lifespan-compare run [Table 23, p.30]. App. J gives 13 entries / 795 tokens (Auto-Dreamer) and 10 entries / 816 tokens (AWM) at episode 80 of find-entity [Table 24, p.31]. [본서 산술] that is 51.1, 66.1, 61.2 and 81.6 tokens per entry respectively. Combined with the retriever's 2048-d embedding [App. B.2, p.18], a per-entry byte estimate is derivable for the first time in the corpus — and it is dominated by the vector, not the text: 2048 dims at fp32 = 8 KB/entry against roughly 50-80 tokens ≈ 200-320 bytes of text. Any such number must carry [본서 산술]; the paper states neither the storage dtype nor any byte figure.
C_cap.unmeasured: Retired-bank size. The logging schema records 'end-of-run active and retired bank sizes' [App. B.2, p.18] and the region-replacement primitive necessarily produces retired entries, but no retired-bank number is printed. Total storage — the quantity a serving operator pays for — is therefore not reported even in tokens.

rho.detail: The paper runs the multi-round regime that would expose $\rho$ — 23 to 66 consolidation events per stream [본서 산술 from Table 5, p.18 and App. B.2, p.16] — and measures no per-round degradation. There is no round-indexed quality curve for a FIXED bank, no re-consolidation-of-already-consolidated-entries experiment, and no information-retention measurement across rounds.
the_nearest_signals_and_why_none_of_them: AUC over the task stream [§5.1, p.7] is round-adjacent but confounded by learning: it mixes the memory improving with the stream's own difficulty ordering. [본서 산술] on WebArena every arm has AUC above its final SR (Auto-Dreamer 0.628 vs 0.523; No memory 0.527 vs 0.446), i.e. cumulative success fell over the stream — but it fell for the memoryless arm too, so it is task order, not consolidation decay.

The cadence sweep [§5.4, p.9; Fig. 3f, p.8] shows degradation in BOTH directions ($k_{\mathrm{cad}}=1$ too little evidence, $k_{\mathrm{cad}}=20$ 'a larger and noisier working region that strains its context and tool-use budget'), which is a statement about region size, not about accumulated loss.

Pattern 3 [§5.5, p.10] is the paper's only direct evidence of consolidation destroying useful information — the trained policy replaces concrete locations with generic procedures and loses the look_at_obj_in_light family. That is a single-round loss mechanism observed qualitatively, not a rate.
Figures 3c/3d track score and bank size across TRAINING steps, not deployment rounds [§5.4, p.9].
rho.why_it_bites_hardest_here: [note-writer] Region replacement makes forgetting the DEFAULT ('information survives only if it is re-synthesized into the replacement set' [§1, p.2]). A mechanism whose stated design property is omission-based forgetting, run for dozens of rounds, with no retention measurement, leaves the corpus's $\rho$ column empty in the one paper best positioned to fill it.

N_q.value: not applicable in the paper's framing, and this is itself a finding
N_q.detail: There is no context shared by $N_q$ queries here. The amortisation object is an experience stream, and the sleep output serves an open-ended future of unrelated tasks. Identity (A) does not have a denominator to fill: the paper never asks how many future queries a consolidation event pays for. [note-writer] For ch25 this is a new regime — the E-path's amortisation argument as ch14/ch15 stated it (one context, several queries) does not describe this system at all, and the paper offers no replacement accounting.

scale_ceiling.model_size: Consolidator Qwen3-14B; task agent Qwen3.5-9B (open-weight) or Gemini-3-flash-preview (undisclosed); writer Qwen3-14B or Gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview; embedder Qwen2.5-3B, 2048-d. The largest trained object in the paper is 14B, and it is the write operator, not the reader [§5.1, p.6; §4.3, p.6; App. B.2, p.18].
scale_ceiling.training_scale: 200 GRPO steps, batch 16 prompts, group size 8, 8×H100 80GB, one environment (ScienceWorld), one seed (42). No token or hour budget is reported [Table 6, p.19].
scale_ceiling.evaluation_scale: 274 ALFWorld tasks (6 families), 660 ScienceWorld tasks (7 of the environment's 30 task types), 117 WebArena tasks (3 of 5 sites). Against the released splits this is 274/274, 660/1802 and 117/812 [Table 5, p.18; Table 7, p.20]. Panel B's held-out set size is never stated.
scale_ceiling.stream_length_ceiling: The longest continual stream is 660 tasks with a consolidation event every 10 sessions, i.e. [본서 산술] roughly 66 rounds. This is by a wide margin the deepest multi-round (U-E) regime in the corpus — ch14's paper ran exactly one round — but it is still a single run per method with no repetition.
scale_ceiling.state_size_ceiling: Banks up to 370,874 tokens (LightMem on WebArena) are exercised as baselines; Auto-Dreamer's own banks stay between 539 and 10,954 tokens. No bank in the paper approaches the per-user scale a deployed assistant would accumulate, and no per-user or cross-run persistence is tested (`run_id`-partitioned storage) [Table 1, p.7; App. B.2, p.18].
scale_ceiling.domain_ceiling_stated_by_the_authors: 'Our evaluation is restricted to three text-based agent environments sharing an LLM-mediated interface (ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, WebArena). We make no claims about transfer to settings with structured state representations, non-textual observations [1], or domains where memory must encode visual or multimodal evidence.' [App. A, p.15]
scale_ceiling.retrieval_regime_ceiling_stated_by_the_a: 'Our main evaluation uses top-K=3 retrieval with a token cap on retrieved entries. This regime favors compact banks; methods that benefit from larger retrieval budgets may rank differently under looser constraints. Characterizing how the Pareto frontier shifts with the retrieval budget is left to future work.' [App. A, p.15]
scale_ceiling.statistical_ceiling: One run per method; bootstrap over tasks only. 'We report point estimates without seed or task-order variance. Several margins in Table 1, particularly on ALFWorld, are small enough that variance estimates would be useful for interpretation.' [App. A, p.15] — in a design whose entire protocol is a single seeded task ORDER.
scale_ceiling.deployment_gap: [note-writer] No real users, no production system, no persistence across runs, no multi-tenant store, no cost figure. The paper's Impact Statement says so: 'It does not introduce a new deployed system… All experiments are conducted in simulated agentic environments… that do not involve personal data or interaction with real users.' [App. D, p.20]

discriminant_verdict.overall: PASS — all four conditions are satisfied. The paper joins group A on the $E$-path, making the census 10 pass + 1 boundary (MemGPT) + 19 not-satisfied = 30. The condition that DECIDES the outcome is (3): which layer's state actually changes at sleep time. Read carelessly — 'trained with GRPO' — this paper files under $\Theta$; read at source it is unambiguously $E$.

conditions.condition: (1) the compute happens BEFORE the query $q$ arrives
conditions.verdict: PASS, in both experimental regimes, and more strictly than the corpus's boundary case
conditions.evidence: Fixed-bank regime: 'The consolidator is invoked exactly once on $\mathcal{B}_0$, producing a consolidated bank $\mathcal{B}^\star$. We then evaluate the frozen task agent equipped with $\mathcal{B}^\star$ on a held-out task set' [§5.3, p.8] — consolidation entirely precedes every query. Continual regime: the prequential protocol places the consolidator strictly between sessions — 'before task t, the agent retrieves from the bank built from tasks 1,…,t−1, and after the task its trajectory is fed to the writer (and, on cadence, to the dreamer) so that future tasks see whatever new entries this trajectory produced' [App. B.2, p.16]. No consolidation occurs during a session.
conditions.comparison_to_the_boundary_case: ch13 records that MemGPT fails condition (1) because its writes happen DURING the conversation. Auto-Dreamer's fast writer also fires after a session rather than during it, and the consolidator fires only every $k_{\mathrm{cad}}$ sessions. Both clocks are between-query. The nearest corpus analogue is ReasoningBank ('after task completion'), which the census counts as a pass.

conditions.verdict: PASS on the condition; the VALUE is absent
conditions.evidence: The consolidator is a 14B model executing a bounded multi-step tool-use rollout with retrieval, entry inspection, raw-trajectory reading and synthesis, fired 23-66 times per stream [§4.1, p.4-5; App. E.2, p.23; App. B.2, p.16]. $B_s$ is self-evidently positive and is in fact the largest sleep-side compute of any $E$-path paper in the corpus. But no FLOP, token, wall-clock or dollar figure is printed anywhere (see cost_table.B_s), even though App. B.2 states that per-role LLM call and token counts are logged.
conditions.note: [note-writer] The condition asks whether a budget is spent, not whether it is reported. Reporting belongs to the cost table. This paper is the cleanest illustration in the corpus of why those are different questions: it passes condition (2) on the strength of a mechanism description alone.

conditions.condition: (3) the state of one of $\Theta$, $W$, $E$ actually changes
conditions.verdict: PASS — and this is THE DECIDING CONDITION for the path assignment
conditions.evidence: $E$ changes: $E_{k+1}=(E_k\setminus\mathcal{W}_k)\cup\hat c_k$ [Eq. 1, §3, p.4]. $\Theta$ does not: 'The task agent, retriever, writer, memory schema, and token budget are all fixed; only the consolidator parameters are updated during training, and only the memory bank is updated after deployment.' [§4, p.4]; 'Offline consolidation leaves the task agent, retriever, and memory schema fixed; it transforms $\mathcal{B}$ into a post-consolidation bank $\mathcal{B}^\star$.' [§3, p.3-4]. $W$ does not exist in these architectures. The rewrite target is a memory region; therefore (U-E), and $\Theta$ is still.
conditions.the_refinement_this_paper_forces_on_the_: Condition (3) asks which layer's STATE moves. It is silent about whether the OPERATOR that moves it has parameters. Auto-Dreamer moves $\theta_C$ — the write operator's own weights — by AdamW/GRPO, on a 14B model, in an offline phase that ends before any evaluation begins [§4.3, p.6; Table 6, p.19]. That is a gradient update with the shape of (U-$\Theta$) applied to a model that is not on the read path. The discriminant handles it correctly because it is scoped to what changes at sleep time within the deployed system; but the book's $E$-path definition ('(U-E)만 실행. $\Theta,W$ 불변', STC-STYLE-NOTATION §1.6) should now be read as a statement about the SERVING artefacts, not about the absence of gradients from the system as a whole. A one-line amendment, not a reclassification.
conditions.counterfactual: Had the paper's GRPO instead updated the TASK AGENT from consolidated memory, it would be a $\Theta$-path paper (SEAL's shape). It does not; the task agent is frozen in every experiment including the ablations.

conditions.condition: (4) the change is used by SUBSEQUENT queries
conditions.verdict: PASS, and it is the evaluation target rather than an incidental property
conditions.evidence: $\mathrm{Read}(q;E^\star)$ by the frozen task agent [Eq. 1, §3, p.4], with retrieved entries injected as '=== Memory from past experience === … === End Memory ===' appended to the env-native system prompt [App. B.2, p.18]. The entire reward and every reported metric is downstream task success on later tasks, and the training reward is literally the return of a frozen agent equipped with the rewritten set [Eq. 3, §4.3, p.6].

discriminant_verdict.which_condition_decides: Condition (3). Conditions (1), (2) and (4) are satisfied by any reasonable reading and were never in doubt. Condition (3) is where the paper could have been misfiled in either direction — as $\Theta$-path because it trains a 14B model with GRPO, or as not-sleep-time-compute at all because 'the memory is just a text bank'. The single sentence at §4, p.4 resolves it: the trained parameters are the write operator's, the deployed update is the bank's. Layer $E$, rule (U-E), operator learned.
discriminant_verdict.secondary_note_for_ch11_ch24: This is the first corpus paper for which condition (3) must be applied TWICE — once to the serving loop (answer: $E$) and once to the pre-deployment loop (answer: $\theta_C$, which is not one of the three layers because it is not part of the model that answers). If more papers train their write operators, the census will need a column for 'is $\mathrm{wr}$ learned?' that is orthogonal to the path assignment.

book_impact.summary: One threat, three confirmations, two gap-fills, one curriculum consequence, and one count change. The threat is real but does not overturn the verdict it targets, because the decisive comparator that ch27 names is absent from this paper.

items.the_book_s_words: '판정 2 — $E$-경로는 유망하다. 단 비용 방법으로서다. 품질 방법으로서는 현재 문헌이 지지하지 않으며, 그 반증은 이 책이 아니라 논문들 자신의 표에서 나온다.' Supporting item A2: '그 6편의 자기 표를 읽으면 품질 1위가 반복적으로 기억 시스템이 없는 구성이다.'
items.what_this_paper_does_to_it: Auto-Dreamer is the first corpus paper in which an $E$-path memory system is the quality winner by a margin its own bootstrap intervals resolve. ScienceWorld: 41.07 [37.53, 44.70] against No memory 28.69 [25.18, 32.14] — non-overlapping. ALFWorld: 60.21 [54.65, 65.59] against No memory 30.83 [26.40, 35.31] — non-overlapping. Panel B: 72.7 vs 24.5 and 44.3 vs 29.6. A2's 'repeatedly' now has a counterexample, and it is a counterexample in the quality column, not the cost column.
items.why_the_verdict_nevertheless_survives: ch27's falsifier FE2 sets three requirements and this paper meets one. (i) 'full-context 팔이 있어야 하고' — there is NO full-context arm; whole-text grep for 'full-context'/'full context' returns 0 hits. The comparator is 'No memory' (instruction + current observation only [App. B.1, p.15]), which is the opposite extreme from full-context, and under a top-$k=3$/1500-token retrieval cap a full-context arm is structurally excluded from the design. (ii) '신뢰구간과 시드가 인쇄되어야 하며' — bootstrap CIs over tasks ARE printed [Table 22, p.29], but seeds are not: 'We report point estimates without seed or task-order variance' [App. A, p.15]. Half met. (iii) '대화 길이가 최소 세 수준으로 스윕되어야 한다' — not done; the swept axis is consolidation cadence, and the retrieval budget, the axis the authors themselves flag as favouring their method, is fixed at one level. So FE2 does not fire. **판정 2 stands, and the reason it stands is precisely the reason ch27 wrote FE2 that way.**
items.the_required_edit: 판정 2's quality clause must acquire a regime qualifier. Its evidence (Mem0's $J$, Zep's DMR, SCM, ReasoningBank) all comes from conversational QA over a single retrievable history, where full-context is both feasible and strong. Auto-Dreamer's regime is a multi-session agentic task stream where the accumulated bank reaches 370k tokens and where the alternative to memory is not full-context but amnesia. The honest form is: in the conversational-QA regime the quality winner is repeatedly the no-memory-system baseline, and no paper has yet run a full-context arm in the agentic-stream regime — so the quality claim is unsupported in one regime and untested in the other.

items.chapter: ch15 §15.6 and PRE-RESEARCH §3.1 (the silence map) / ch14 bridge chain
items.relation: PARTIALLY OVERTURNS the intra-path silence finding; CONFIRMS the cross-path silence finding
items.detail: Intra-path: ch15 records that none of the five successors cites ch14's paper, and ch14 had to be written as an inheritance-free start. Auto-Dreamer cites Letta STC [ref 14], names LightMem as its closest architectural counterpart, and executes the multi-round regime Letta STC deferred. The $E$-path chain now has a third link that holds, and the book's statement that the founding paper is uncited by its own successors must be dated rather than stated in the present tense. Cross-path: total silence persists and is now unambiguously chosen rather than chronological — whole-text greps return 'KV' 0, 'fast weight' 0, 'test-time training' 0, 'Titans' 0, 'LoRA' 0, 'fine-tun' 0, 'gradient' 0. In a May 2026 paper with 45 references, not one W-path or $\Theta$-path memory method appears. The book's 표 27-4 row '$\Theta$ | 검색($E$-경로) | 실행되지 않았다' gains its mirror image: the $E$-path frontier does not run a $\Theta$-path or $W$-path baseline either.

items.chapter: ch26 finding E1 and 판정 1; ch26 falsifier R-1
items.relation: CONFIRMS the letter of E1 while materially weakening its force; moves R-1 one step closer
items.detail: E1 — no discriminant-passing paper reports $C_{\text{cap}}$ in per-user or per-session bytes — SURVIVES: Auto-Dreamer reports tokens, not bytes, and per run, not per user. But it is the first corpus paper to print a state-size column at all, for eleven systems across three domains, beside the quality number, in units that are common across systems [Table 1, p.7]. R-1 asks for 'a report printing two or more paths' per-user state in the same unit'; this is one path's eleven systems in one unit, which does not fire R-1 but does end the corpus's total silence on capacity. ch26 must record both halves: the letter of E1 holds, and the sentence 'corpus 전체에서 상태 용량을 바이트로 보고한 논문이 0편이다' should be tightened to say 'in bytes, per user' so that it does not read as denying what this table contains. The paper also supplies, for the first time, the entry-count and embedding-dimension data (2048-d) needed to derive bytes per entry — with the finding that the vector dominates the text by roughly an order of magnitude [본서 산술].

items.relation: OPENS A REGIME THE ACCOUNTING DOES NOT COVER
items.detail: ch25's structural defect in the $E$-path amortisation argument is that the per-query prompt term does not divide by $N_q$. Auto-Dreamer has no $N_q$ at all: there is no context shared by a known number of queries, and the sleep output serves an open-ended stream of unrelated future tasks. Simultaneously, its per-query prompt term is CAPPED BY CONSTRUCTION (top-3, 1500 tokens, identical for every arm), so bank size never enters the wake prompt. Both of ch25's terms therefore behave differently here, and the paper supplies no substitute accounting. For ch28's $B_s$ axis the paper is a negative data point of the sharpest kind: it logs per-role token counts [App. B.2, p.18] and prints none, so it belongs in the audit as 'measured and withheld' rather than 'not measured'.

items.chapter: ch05 (RL for LLM), ch07 (forgetting and replay), and the ch14 note's teaching claim
items.detail: The ch14 note recorded that the $E$-path is the cleanest entry point to the three-layer frame because it can be demonstrated without a single backward pass. That is no longer true of the path's frontier: GRPO, group-relative advantage, reward shaping and a counterfactual credit term are all required to read this paper. ch05 acquires an $E$-path consumer alongside SEAL and ReasoningBank. ch07 acquires an $E$-path instance of omission-based forgetting as a DESIGNED property rather than a failure mode — 'information survives only if it is re-synthesized into the replacement set' [§1, p.2] — together with the paper's own demonstration that it can destroy useful information (Pattern 3, §5.5, p.10).

The cheapest observation that would move 판정 2 in the agentic-stream regime is now specifiable exactly: rerun this paper's Table 1 with (a) a full-context or full-bank arm at whatever retrieval budget admits it, (b) the retrieval budget swept over at least three levels, and (c) three seeds and three task orders. All three are configuration changes to an existing harness — no new method, no new benchmark. The paper itself names (b) as future work [App. A, p.15] and admits the current regime 'favors compact banks'.

items.chapter: ch18, ch19, ch20, ch21, ch22, ch16, ch17, ch12, ch08, ch29
items.detail: The paper contains no $W$-path or $\Theta$-path mechanism, no weight editing, no LoRA, no continual-learning method, no capacity theory, and no serving or hardware measurement. It does not cite Nested Learning, Memory Caching, Generative Adapter, SEAL, ROME/MEMIT, EWC, or any biological sleep experiment beyond the three CLS theory papers. ch29's memory-device argument gains nothing: there is no byte figure, no hierarchy discussion, and no latency measurement in the paper.

new_concepts_this_paper_introduces.why_it_matters_to_the_book: a fourth $\mathrm{wr}$ species, and the first whose stated design goal is that forgetting be the DEFAULT rather than a decision

new_concepts_this_paper_introduces.definition: the rewrite unit: entries written during the last $k_{\mathrm{cad}}$ sessions plus older entries retrieved by the task agent in the same interval

each entry carries pointers to the raw action-observation traces that produced it; the consolidator may re-read them via `get_source_trace` while the task agent cannot. Fan-in = the number of source entries cited by one synthesized entry.
the expected performance drop under random masking of a fraction $\rho_{\mathrm{mask}}$ of the synthesized set; positive for load-bearing entries, near zero for duplicates, negative for harmful ones
scoring a candidate replacement set as if it were the entire store, so that credit attaches to the rollout's own output rather than to a bank containing other memories
the paper's two evaluation regimes — a growing bank over a prequential stream, and one rewrite of an identical pre-built bank followed by held-out evaluation
new_concepts_this_paper_introduces.why_it_matters_to_the_book: the second is the cleanest isolation of the write operator anywhere in the $E$-path corpus and is the design ch27's FE2 should be written against

new_concepts_this_paper_introduces.definition: a deliberately handicapped per-session writer paired with a cross-session consolidator that owns all merging, abstraction, correction, compression and forgetting

open_questions.question: How should bank structure be maintained beyond a single working region per event, and can retrieval and consolidation be optimised jointly?
open_questions.exact_wording: 'The current consolidator rewrites one working region per consolidation event; future work could maintain longer-range bank structure, jointly optimize retrieval and consolidation, or handle multimodal source trajectories.'
open_questions.bridge_out: the unswept tail of AD3 — entries never retrieved are never reconsidered — is the concrete form of this question

open_questions.question: How does the success-cost Pareto frontier move with the retrieval budget?
open_questions.exact_wording: 'Our main evaluation uses top-K=3 retrieval with a token cap on retrieved entries. This regime favors compact banks; methods that benefit from larger retrieval budgets may rank differently under looser constraints. Characterizing how the Pareto frontier shifts with the retrieval budget is left to future work.'
open_questions.bridge_out: this is the paper's own admission that its central axis is regime-dependent, and it is the first of ch27's FE2 requirements

open_questions.question: What is the formal relationship between local-bank ranking at training time and full-bank ranking at deployment?
open_questions.exact_wording: 'The local-bank training objective (§4.3) is a surrogate for deployment-time bank composition. While our online experiments show that the surrogate transfers, the formal relationship between local-bank ranking and full-bank ranking is not characterized.'

open_questions.question: Is the consolidator robust to a different writer, a different schema, or noisier provenance links?
open_questions.exact_wording: 'The consolidator operates over entries written by a fixed prompted writer with a specific semantic/procedural schema. We hold these constant to isolate the consolidator, but robustness to alternative writers, schemas, or noisier provenance links remains untested. Information missed by the writer cannot generally be recovered by the consolidator unless source trajectories make it salient.'
open_questions.bridge_out: the last clause is a bound on the whole two-timescale design: the slow system cannot exceed the union of what the fast system recorded and what the traces expose

open_questions.question: How large are the margins relative to seed and task-order variance?
open_questions.exact_wording: 'We report point estimates without seed or task-order variance. Several margins in Table 1, particularly on ALFWorld, are small enough that variance estimates would be useful for interpretation.'

open_questions.question: How should a learned consolidator be prevented from over-compressing locally useful specifics?
open_questions.status: identified as the paper's own failure mode (Pattern 3) with a mechanism story and no proposed fix: 'the learned policy can over-compress specific facts that are locally useful'

open_questions.question: What does consolidation cost?
open_questions.status: not asked by the paper. $B_s$, wall-clock and dollars are absent although logged (see cost_table.B_s). [note-writer] this is a question the paper does not pose rather than one it leaves open.

open_questions.question: How does quality degrade across many consolidation rounds on a fixed underlying experience set?
open_questions.status: not asked. The paper runs 23-66 rounds and measures no retention.
open_questions.source: [본서 관찰 from Table 5 p.18 and App. B.2 p.16]

open_questions.question: Does the reward oracle requirement survive deployment?
open_questions.status: not discussed. Training scores candidate banks by running a frozen agent on evaluation tasks drawn from the training environment [§3, p.4; Eq. 3, p.6], i.e. it needs an environment with a gold return signal. What happens where no such environment exists is never raised — and this is the same oracle problem ch20 identified for SEAL, now appearing on the $E$-path.

unfavorable_facts.fact: No compute cost of any kind is reported, and the paper's own logs contain it. 'latency' occurs 0 times in the whole text; 'FLOP' 0; 'GPU-hour' 0; 'dollar' 0; 'seconds' 0. All seven occurrences of 'cost' refer to memory-bank size in tokens.
unfavorable_facts.the_sharp_part: App. B.2 (p.18) states that `summary.json` reports 'total wall-clock time, and per-role LLM call and token counts' and that `dreamer_calls.jsonl` logs dreamer events. The sleep-side budget was measured and not printed.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the paper's thesis is a success-cost tradeoff and only one of the two axes is a cost

unfavorable_facts.fact: The quantity the paper calls 'retrieval-time memory cost' is not a retrieval-time cost. Retrieval is capped at top-$k=3$ under a 1500-token budget for every arm, plus top-1 every 8 environment steps.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: under the paper's own protocol a 370,874-token bank and a 927-token bank inject the same bounded number of tokens per query, so the 12× and 6× 'less memory' figures are storage ratios, not serving-cost ratios. The label appears in §5.2 (p.8) and in the Fig. 3 caption (p.8).
unfavorable_facts.source: [§5.2, p.8; Fig. 3 caption, p.8; App. B.2, p.18]

unfavorable_facts.fact: The WebArena result is statistically null and the paper presents it as a win. Auto-Dreamer 52.3 [43.5, 60.9] against No memory 44.6 [36.0, 53.2] — the point estimate lies INSIDE the memoryless interval. AWM reaches 52.0 [43.1, 60.8] with a SMALLER bank (890 vs 927 tokens); LightMem also reaches 52.0.
unfavorable_facts.the_paper_s_claim: 'on WebArena, where it obtains the highest SR despite the longer-horizon tasks and noisier accessibility-tree observations' [§5.2, p.8]; the abstract says it 'continues to lead on held-out ALFWorld and WebArena'.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: WebArena is one of the two held-out domains carrying the transfer claim, and it is the domain where the two strongest RL baselines were not run at all
unfavorable_facts.source: [Table 1 Panel A, p.7; Table 22, p.29; §5.2, p.8]

unfavorable_facts.fact: The ALFWorld lead is not resolved by the paper's own intervals. Auto-Dreamer 60.21 [54.65, 65.59], UMEM 58.43 [53.15, 63.65], Mem-α 57.40 [52.04, 62.59].
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: ALFWorld is the other held-out domain; the transfer claim rests on two domains, one indistinguishable from the baselines and one indistinguishable from no memory

unfavorable_facts.fact: Only the in-domain gap is clean, and even it is not clean against the strongest baseline. On ScienceWorld — the TRAINING environment — Auto-Dreamer [37.53, 44.70] and UMEM [30.51, 37.71] still overlap by 0.18pp; no paired test is run. On ScienceWorld the interval does clear No memory [25.18, 32.14].
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the headline '+7 points over the strongest baseline' is stated without reference to Table 22, which is never cited in §5

unfavorable_facts.fact: There is no full-context or full-bank baseline anywhere. Whole-text grep for 'full-context' and 'full context' returns 0 hits. The only memoryless comparator receives 'only the current observation and the task instruction'.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the one comparison that would settle whether consolidation beats simply having everything available is absent, and the retrieval regime (top-3, 1500 tokens) excludes it by construction. This is the reason ch27's 판정 2 survives the paper.
unfavorable_facts.source: [whole-text grep; App. B.1, p.15; App. B.2, p.18]

unfavorable_facts.fact: The authors state that their evaluation regime favours their method and do not run the alternative. 'Our main evaluation uses top-K=3 retrieval with a token cap on retrieved entries. This regime favors compact banks; methods that benefit from larger retrieval budgets may rank differently under looser constraints.'
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: compactness is the paper's headline property and the evaluation is admitted to be biased toward it

unfavorable_facts.fact: 'Panel B of Table 1 reproduces the online ranking' is contradicted by Table 1. [본서 관찰] ALFWorld A→B: ExpeL 5th→2nd, Memp 7th→3rd, Mem0 11th→5th, UMEM 2nd→7th, Reflexion 4th→8th. ScienceWorld A→B: Mem0 11th→2nd, ExpeL 9th→4th, ReasoningBank 3rd→11th, UMEM 2nd→9th. Only rank 1 is reproduced.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the controlled study is offered as corroboration of the online ranking; what it corroborates is one row of it
unfavorable_facts.source: [§5.3, p.8; Table 1 Panels A and B, p.7]

unfavorable_facts.fact: GRPO's contribution is large only in the environment it was trained on. [본서 산술] trained minus untrained: ScienceWorld +9.7pp (training env), ALFWorld +1.0pp, WebArena +5.7pp — against Table 22 half-widths of about ±3.6, ±5.5 and ±8.7pp on the same protocol. Table 2 carries no intervals.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the paper's second headline is that the LEARNED operator transfers; the two out-of-domain training gains are inside the paper's own noise scale

unfavorable_facts.fact: On ALFWorld, training makes the bank BIGGER for +1.0pp: untrained 6,900 tokens → trained 10,954 tokens, a 59% increase.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: compactness is attributed to the primitive and quality to the learning, but on this domain the learning costs compactness and buys almost no quality

unfavorable_facts.fact: The ALFWorld trained-vs-untrained margin is restated after removing the adverse task family. '+1.0pp' becomes '+4.9pp (65.8 vs. 60.9)' once look_at_obj_in_light is excluded, and the exclusion is justified by the mechanism it exposes.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the excluded family is the one where the paper's own method is worse than its own ablation; the widened figure appears twice (§5.4 and §5.5) and the aggregate only once

unfavorable_facts.fact: The reward that was optimised is not the reward that is printed. Eq. 2 is $r_g=U_{\mathcal{V}}+\alpha r_{\mathrm{cf}}$, but Table 6 lists 'Format-penalty weight 0.5' under Reward shaping — a third term appearing in no equation.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the reward is the paper's methodological core and its printed form is incomplete

unfavorable_facts.fact: Every baseline is a re-implementation with disclosed deviations from its published configuration. All ten share a swapped encoder (Qwen2.5-3B); ReasoningBank's LLM-as-Judge is replaced by the environment's gold reward and MaTTS scaling is 'not implemented'; LightMem's topic segmentation is 'not replicated'; Mem0's current pipeline is 'bypassed' for legacy commit prompts; AWM's read() ignores the encoder and prepends the whole library; ExpeL's few-shot count is raised from 2 to 10; Reflexion is 'adapted to a cross-task-type reflection-transfer regime'.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: the disclosure is unusually honest and complete, and it also means no baseline number here is that method's published number
unfavorable_facts.source: [Table 3, p.17; Table 4, p.17; App. B.1.6, p.16]

unfavorable_facts.fact: The two strongest baselines are absent from one of three domains, and it is the domain where the margin is smallest. Mem-α and UMEM are omitted on WebArena because their memory-optimizer context windows cannot hold accessibility-tree observations plus the bank; the authors decline to retrain with larger backbones on compute grounds.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: on WebArena the reported comparison set excludes precisely the arms that beat every prompted baseline on ALFWorld

unfavorable_facts.fact: One seed, one task order, in a protocol whose entire structure is a single seeded task order. 'We report point estimates without seed or task-order variance.' Bootstrap resampling of tasks does not estimate order variance, and order determines which entries exist when.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: for a prequential design the task order is not a nuisance parameter, it is an input to the mechanism

unfavorable_facts.fact: $\rho$ is unmeasured in the paper best positioned to measure it. Region replacement makes omission the default ('information survives only if it is re-synthesized'), the consolidator fires 23-66 times per stream, and no retention or degradation quantity is reported at any round.

Total storage is never reported even in tokens. The logging schema records 'end-of-run active and retired bank sizes' [App. B.2, p.18] and region replacement necessarily retires entries, but only ACTIVE size is printed. The quantity an operator pays for is the sum.

Coverage inside the training environment is partial and the split statistics disagree with the evaluation pool. ScienceWorld has 30 task types [Table 7, p.20]; evaluation samples 7 [Table 5, p.18]. WebArena has 5 sites [Table 7, p.20]; evaluation uses 3 [Table 5, p.18; App. C.3, p.20]. ScienceWorld's released test split is 1,802 tasks; 660 are used. WebArena's is 812; 117 are used.

The appendix case study's 'compact steady state' does not compose with the main result. App. I reports 14 entries / 716 tokens and 'a compact steady state of roughly 10–14 active entries within the first half of the stream'; the main ScienceWorld run ends at 6,947 tokens, which at App. I's own 51.1 tokens/entry is roughly 136 entries.
unfavorable_facts.hedge: the case study may be a separate 96-episode single-category run and entry length may differ; recorded as a composition question — see todo_verify
unfavorable_facts.source: [App. I and Table 23, pp.29-30; Table 1, p.7]

unfavorable_facts.fact: Prompt engineering was tuned on observed outcomes and reported as a design fact, not ablated. The WebArena writer's failure prompt excludes behavioural failure entries because 'we observed that behavioral failure entries ... generalize net-negative'; memory-aware task-agent prompt variants were 'found to be net-negative on the final aggregate score' and dropped; and the appendix prompts were reproduced 'after stripping a small number of defensive phrases that we found contributed nothing to performance'.
unfavorable_facts.why_it_bites: three outcome-informed prompt decisions, none of them quantified, all inside the arm that wins
unfavorable_facts.source: [App. E preamble, p.20; App. E.1.3, p.22]

unfavorable_facts.fact: The abstract's 'active memory bank 12× smaller than the strongest baseline' is a ratio against the strongest-by-SR baseline, not the smallest bank. [본서 관찰] AWM's ScienceWorld bank is 3,877 tokens against Auto-Dreamer's 6,947; ExpeL's ALFWorld bank is 2,042 against 10,954; AWM's WebArena bank is 890 against 927.
unfavorable_facts.status: correct as written; recorded because the Fig. 3a Pareto framing invites the stronger reading

unfavorable_facts.fact: No artefact release. Despite recording internal file paths and per-baseline commit hashes as if the code were public [App. B.1.6, p.16], no repository URL for Auto-Dreamer appears anywhere in the paper.

The provenance fan-in claim does not match its own axis. §5.5 says the distribution 'peaks at fan-in = 5' while the vendored figure's bins read 1 / 2-3 / 4-5 / 6-9 / 10+, which cannot have a peak at exactly 5.
unfavorable_facts.hedge: figure-derived from an OCR'd axis; must be checked against the PDF before assertion — see todo_verify

cross_path_citations.verdict: Deep engagement with the $E$-path and with RL-for-memory; total silence toward the $W$-path and toward $\Theta$-path memory; and — a first for this path — a real, sourced CLS citation accompanied by an explicit refusal of the biological claim.

E_path_internal.citations: the densest in the corpus. Atomic/flat stores: A-MEM [34], Mem0 [2], MemOS [13], SimpleMem [15]. Typed stores: EverMemOS [9], MIRIX [29], Nemori [19], PlugMem [36]. Procedural/skill: Memp [6], Voyager [26], AWM [31]. Insight extraction: ExpeL [42], ReasoningBank [20], Reflexion [23], Self-Refine [16]. Episodic retrieval: MemoryBank [43], MemGPT [21]. Test-time memory evolution: Evo-Memory/ReMem [32]. Two surveys [10, 11].
E_path_internal.the_founding_paper: Letta `Sleep-time Compute` [14] IS cited — once, in §2 'Offline computation and sleep-time memory' (p.3): 'Sleep-time compute [14] pre-computes over persistent context before queries arrive, amortizing reasoning across future interactions.' This is the first citation of ch14's paper by any $E$-path successor in the extended corpus.
E_path_internal.finding: [note-writer] ch15's finding that none of the five successors cites the founding paper must now be dated. The chain founder → LightMem → Auto-Dreamer holds, with the mechanism difference named at each link.

RL_for_memory.citations: MEM1 [45], MemAgent [38], Memory-R1 [35], Learn-to-Memorize [41], REMEMBER [39], Mem-α [30], UMEM [37], MemRL [40] — and two of them (Mem-α, UMEM) are run as baselines rather than merely cited. GRPO itself via DeepSeekMath [22].
RL_for_memory.finding: This is a literature the book's corpus does not contain at all. Auto-Dreamer sits at its junction with the $E$-path, and the junction is where the paper's novelty lives.

W_path.citations: ZERO. Whole-text greps: 'KV' 0, 'fast weight' 0, 'test-time training' 0, 'Titans' 0. No linear attention, no state-space model, no recurrent memory, no Memory Caching, no Nested Learning, no fast-weight programmer.
W_path.finding: chronology forces none of this. Every W-path paper in the corpus predates May 2026.

Theta_path.citations: ZERO memory-in-weights. Greps: 'LoRA' 0, 'fine-tun' 0, 'gradient' 0. No PEFT, no ROME/MEMIT, no SEAL, no continual learning, no catastrophic forgetting, no distillation. The one Θ-shaped citation, DeepSeekMath [22], is the RL algorithm used to train the write operator, not a memory method.
Theta_path.the_irony: [note-writer] the paper performs a gradient update on a 14B model and cites no work on putting knowledge into weights. It uses (U-$\Theta$) machinery while ignoring the entire (U-$\Theta$) memory literature.

bio_CLS.citations: THREE, at the primary sources: McClelland, McNaughton & O'Reilly 1995 [17]; Kumaran, Hassabis & McClelland 2016 [12]; McClelland, McNaughton & Lampinen 2020 [18].
bio_CLS.the_disclaimer: 'We adopt CLS not as a biological claim about language models, but as an operational design principle for separating fast acquisition from slow cross-session consolidation.' [§1, p.2]
bio_CLS.what_is_still_absent: no hippocampal-replay experiment, no sleep-consolidation neuroscience, no dreaming literature (PLOS and PAD are absent), no EWC/DGR/GEM. The citation is to CLS THEORY only.
bio_CLS.finding: the first E-path paper in the corpus to cite CLS at all, and it prints the caveat ch23 §23.8 exists to demand. It also does not reuse the word 'sleep' for its own mechanism.

sleep_time_compute_as_a_name.usage: 'sleep' appears twice in the body, both in the §2 sentence describing Letta STC (p.3). The paper's own mechanism is never called sleep-time compute; it is called 'offline memory consolidation'.
sleep_time_compute_as_a_name.finding: [note-writer] evidence for ch24's 판정 2 falsifier F6, which watches whether later papers converge on the name. This paper does the opposite and arguably better: it recognises the category, cites its founder, and picks a name that states the layer and the clock.

cross_path_citations.monograph_implication: [note-writer] The silence map (PRE-RESEARCH §3.1) gains a row where the intra-path column flips to ○ while the $W$ and $\Theta$ columns stay ✗ in a 2026 paper with 45 references. That is the cleanest available demonstration that the cross-path gap is chosen rather than chronological — the $E$-path can and does read across, just not across paths.

systems_implications.preamble: Grounding key: [PAPER] = on the page with a locator; [본서 산술] = arithmetic from the paper's numbers; [본서 추론] = deduced, not claimed by the paper. This paper reports far fewer systems numbers than its framing suggests — it has a state-size axis and no time or compute axis at all.

items.claim: Nothing in the decode kernel changes. The wake-time request is an ordinary request with a bounded memory panel appended to the system prompt and top-1 entries appended to user messages mid-episode.
items.grounding: [PAPER] App. B.2, p.18: retrieved entries 'injected as raw INSERT_* blocks inside a === Memory from past experience === ... === End Memory === panel appended to the env-native system prompt'.

items.claim: Shared-weight batching is preserved absolutely. No per-user, per-session or per-run weight state exists anywhere in the serving path.
items.grounding: [PAPER] §4, p.4 (everything frozen). [본서 추론] for the batching consequence. This is ch27's A5 advantage, and this paper does not claim it either — the corpus tally of $E$-path papers arguing their strongest serving point stays at zero.

items.claim: The wake-time memory prompt is capped by construction and is IDENTICAL across arms, so bank size does not buy prefill savings in this design.
items.grounding: [PAPER] App. B.2, p.18: top-$k=3$ under a 1500-token budget at task start, top-1 appended every 8 environment steps; step caps 50/100/300 [Table 5, p.18]. [본서 산술] per-episode injected-memory ceiling is 1500 tokens plus at most 6/12/37 single entries. [본서 추론] the 12× and 6× bank ratios are storage ratios; the serving-time difference they buy is retrieval PRECISION, index size and rerank work — not prompt tokens.

items.claim: Where bank size actually costs: an in-process vector index. 2048-d embeddings from a Qwen2.5-3B encoder, FAISS IndexFlatIP over L2-normalised vectors, persisted in LanceDB partitioned by run_id, with a hybrid kNN plus salience rerank at query time.
items.grounding: [PAPER] App. B.1.6, p.16; App. B.2, p.18. [본서 산술] at fp32 one 2048-d vector is 8 KB; at App. I's 51.1 tokens/entry the entry text is roughly 200 bytes. The embedding dominates the stored bytes by more than an order of magnitude — the first corpus datum from which that can be computed. The paper states no storage dtype, so any absolute must carry [본서 산술].

items.claim: The memory panel is a VARYING suffix of the system prompt, which defeats cross-task prefix caching for every memory arm — and only for the memory arms.
items.grounding: [본서 추론] from App. B.2, p.18 (panel appended to the env-native system prompt at task start, refreshed mid-episode). The No memory arm has an invariant system prompt and is therefore the arm that benefits most from prefix caching. The paper never mentions caching; 'prefix' occurs twice, once as 'ranked prefix' in Eq. 1 and once inside a baseline prompt. This is the same missing switch ch27's A3 records for Mem0 and Zep, pointing the same direction: turning it on helps the baseline.

items.claim: Sleep-side work is a batchable, latency-insensitive agentic decode job fired tens of times per stream, and its throughput requirement is bounded by the cadence.
items.grounding: [PAPER] cadence 10/8/5 sessions [App. B.2, p.16]; [본서 산술] roughly 66/34/23 events per stream at the pool sizes of Table 5. Each event is a sequential multi-turn rollout by a 14B model with tool calls, so wall-clock per event is not small even off the critical path — and the paper reports neither turns used nor time taken.

items.claim: The serving path needs THREE models plus an index, and the paper says so operationally: task agent, writer, consolidator and embedder are served as four independent endpoints on one node.
items.grounding: [PAPER] App. B.2 'Models served' and 'Hardware', p.18: 'Open-weight roles (task agent, writer when Qwen, dreamer, embedder) are served as independent SGLang endpoints on the same evaluation node'; evaluation on 4×GH200 96GB. [본서 추론] the memory subsystem's resident footprint (14B writer + 14B consolidator + 3B embedder) exceeds the 9B task agent that actually answers. No corpus paper has priced that asymmetry.

items.claim: Traffic lands in application storage and never in device memory. Text and 2048-d vectors into LanceDB; nothing into HBM-resident weights, optimizer state or a per-user weight shard.
items.grounding: [PAPER] App. B.2, p.18. [본서 추론] for the hierarchy walk. This is the sharpest available contrast with the $\Theta$-path for ch26/ch29: this path's write traffic is text plus vectors into a database, and no memory-device opportunity arises from it.

items.claim: The one genuinely new serving lever this paper exposes is retrieval-slot efficiency under a FIXED wake budget.
items.grounding: [PAPER] App. I, p.30: at the same 3-slot budget, LightMem 'retrieves the same task-instruction sentence three times, each from a different timestamp' while Auto-Dreamer 'retrieves three distinct pieces of information'. [본서 추론] with the wake budget pinned, the design question becomes information per retrieved token rather than tokens saved — a rate-distortion framing (→ ch22) rather than an amortisation one (→ ch25). The paper does not draw this connection and cites no rate-distortion work.

items.claim: There is no admission-control signal and no allocation policy. Consolidation fires on a fixed session count, never on evidence of need.
items.grounding: [PAPER] §4.2, p.5; App. B.2, p.16. [본서 추론] ch14's paper at least proposed $\log P(q\mid c)$ as a predictability signal; here the only knob is a cadence, and the sweep shows both directions hurt [§5.4, p.9], i.e. the optimum is interior and per-environment with no rule for finding it.

items.claim: Training is the cost that a deployer would actually face first, and it is unpriced. 8×H100 for 200 GRPO steps in which every one of 25,600 rollouts is scored by running a frozen 9B agent through full environment episodes plus masked resamples.
items.grounding: [PAPER] Table 6, p.19; App. B.2 'Hardware', p.18. [본서 산술] for the rollout count. [본서 추론] the environment-in-the-loop reward makes this far more expensive per step than text-only RL, and it requires a gold-return environment — the same oracle dependence ch20 identified for SEAL, now on the $E$-path.
